chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Does the saffron stain the clothes of the person in Ihram from the Kaaba?' He said: 'It does not harm him, and he does not need to wash it.'

And it is not permissible for the person in Ihram to wear a garment that has saffron in its weave, nor to wear a cloak with saffron, nor to wear trousers, unless he does not have an izar (lower garment).

key_terms.إِزَارٌ: A lower garment (loincloth/skirt) worn by men
key_terms.الزَّعْفَرَانُ: Saffron, used here to denote a yellow dye or woven element
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (sacred ritual consecration)
key_terms.يَدَّرِعَهُ: To wear a darr' (a cloak or upper garment)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on wearing clothes stained with saffron during Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between mere staining (*al-zu'ran*) and the fabric being woven with saffron (*yazurruhu*), establishing that incidental contact with the Kaaba's scent does not break the sanctity of Ihram. It further delineates the prohibition of wearing tailored trousers (*sarawil*) or wrapped garments (*darr'*) unless no loose lower garment (*izar*) is available, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on simplicity and the avoidance of specific clothing types during the sacred state. This ruling underscores the principle that Ihram restrictions are lifted only by necessity (*darura*), a key concept in Usuli jurisprudence.
